newsitem.title: MEXICO: Alestra outlines new telephone rates in Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Alestra outlines new telephone rates in Mexico.

text.p: Alestra, a Mexican long-distance company owned by AT&T and Mexican holding company Grupo Industrial Alfa, S.A. released on Sunday its tariff rates for long-distance calls inside Mexico.
Wide-spread competition in the long distance market starts on January 1, 1997 in Mexico.
Alestra said that it would offer long-distance service at a daytime cost of 1.9 pesos. The rate on those calls at night and on weekends will be 0.95 of a peso. These are charges per minute.
The company said this compares with weekday rates of 1.998 pesos for Telmex and 2.0 pesos for Avantel, and night and weekend rates of 0.994 of a peso for Telmex and 1.0 peso for Avantel.
Avantel is a joint venture between MCI Communications Corp and Grupo Financiero Banamex Accival, S.A. DE C.V.
